summary.summary_text: Ceylon Beverage Holdings is a holding company whose principal operating asset is Lion Brewery (Ceylon) PLC; its own standalone revenue is trivial (LKR 1.3Bn company vs LKR 125.2Bn Group in FY2025) and it earns almost entirely through its stake in Lion's beer business plus a small pub-franchise royalty operation, Pubs 'N Places (Annual Report 2022/23, p.9). It is itself a subsidiary of Carson Cumberbatch PLC (Annual Report 2020/21, notes). Because its consolidated figures are Lion Brewery's figures plus minor holding-company items, its Group revenue and profit trends track Lion's almost exactly: revenue grew from LKR 49.2Bn (FY2020) to LKR 125.2Bn (FY2025), roughly 2.5x, on the same excise-duty and devaluation-driven pricing dynamics (Chairman's Statement, FY2021 and FY2023 Annual Reports). The one dependency worth separating from Lion's own profile: as a pure holding structure, BREW's own cash flow depends on dividends upstreamed from Lion, not on any operations it runs directly.
summary.gaps_note: No gaps for FY2020-FY2025 and the latest interim. Note EPS shown is Group basis; BREW's own standalone (Company) EPS is materially lower since almost all Group profit is attributable to Lion Brewery, only partly owned by BREW.

financials_interim.notes: Group basis. Revenue Rs 35,908,055k, PAT Rs 3,250,994k for the quarter ended 30 September 2025 (Statement of Profit or Loss - Group, Quarter Ended column). Note: EPS not separately disclosed at Group level in this statement (only Company-level EPS of Rs 1.81 shown, which reflects only the holding company's own income, not the operating Group); left blank rather than citing the non-comparable Company EPS figure.

financials_annual.notes: Group basis. Comparative-year figures sourced from the same FY2025 annual report (2024 column) as the current-year row, not a separately backfilled FY2024 report. Same statement-page citations apply as the FY2025 row.
Group basis. Operating profit = Profit before finance cost as labelled. D&A summed from cash flow note. Tax = income tax + deferred tax. BS spans p.89-90, CF spans p.96-97.

thesis.thesis_text: Ceylon Beverage Holdings is a holding company whose principal asset is its stake in Lion Brewery (Ceylon) PLC; nearly all of its Group revenue and profit originate at the subsidiary level. FY2025 Group results show double-digit revenue growth (+11.8%) with even faster profit growth (+21.1%), low leverage (debt/equity 0.14x), and a materially lower finance cost burden than FY2024 (interest coverage roughly doubled). At 12.5x trailing P/E with a modest 1.65% dividend yield, the stock is not statistically cheap, but growth and balance-sheet quality both look genuinely improving on a two-year comparison (Annual Report FY2025, p.89, p.91).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/IMF/World Bank/news data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Governance & Risk is also necessarily thin -- no circulars/disclosures feed exists (deliberately disabled this session), so insider transactions, board changes, and rights issues cannot be verified directly; the score below reflects only what's visible in audited financial statements and public market data.

financial_quality.rationale: FY2025 Group ROE 27.6%, ROA 14.9%, current ratio 1.62x, debt/equity just 0.14x -- low leverage, high returns. Net margin thin at 7.7% (beverage distribution has structurally high cost of sales) but interest coverage roughly doubled YoY as finance costs fell 43.8%.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group revenue +11.8% YoY (LKR 111.9bn to 125.2bn), PAT +21.1% YoY (7.98bn to 9.66bn) -- growth is outpacing revenue, implying margin expansion, not just volume growth.

valuation.rationale: P/E 12.5x on trailing Group EPS (LKR 243.82), P/B 1.83x, dividend yield 1.65% with a conservative 20.7% payout ratio (retaining most earnings). Not statistically cheap or expensive for a growing consumer name.

business_quality.rationale: BREW's own standalone entity is a thin holding shell (Company revenue just LKR 1.3bn vs LKR 125.2bn Group) whose real value is its stake in Lion Brewery -- genuine business quality sits with the operating subsidiary, not BREW itself, which caps this score below LION's own.

governance_risk.rationale: Clean, audited Group/Company financials with consistent multi-year filing history. No disclosures feed to verify board/ownership changes independently.

key_reasons: PAT grew 21.1% YoY, outpacing 11.8% revenue growth -- margin expansion, not just volume
Debt/equity of just 0.14x and finance costs down 43.8% YoY -- balance sheet strengthening
Low 20.7% payout ratio signals capacity to raise dividends without straining cash flow
watch_factors: BREW's standalone financials are thin (LKR 1.3bn revenue) -- the real investment case is Lion Brewery's performance, not BREW's own operations
No excise/regulatory tax data tracked -- a Sri Lankan alcohol excise hike would compress margins at the operating subsidiary
Only 2 periods of financials on file (FY2025, FY2024) -- thesis will sharpen once a third year is added

horizon_notes.6m: Near-term view depends on FY2026 interim results tracking the FY2025 margin-expansion trend; no forward guidance verified.
horizon_notes.1y: If Group PAT growth (~20%) persists, current 12.5x P/E would look increasingly reasonable; a slowdown would make it look full.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis is really a bet on Lion Brewery's multi-year execution and export diversification, not BREW's own operations.
horizon_notes.5y: Long-run case rests on sustained beverage demand growth and continued deleveraging; no 5-year data on file to verify a trend at this horizon.
